result_text:
Northgate Clinic is one customer under two account IDs. It was ACC-1042 through 2026-03-31 and became ACC-1077, "Northgate Health Partners (formerly Northgate Clinic)", on 2026-04-01. I combined the two. The only link between them is the "formerly" in the account name, so I'm assuming that is the same customer.

**Plan and pricing**
- It moved from `standard` to `enterprise-annual` effective 2026-03-01, and the plan stayed the same after the rename.
- The effective rate per billed unit fell from $0.42 on standard to $0.31 on enterprise-annual (e.g. 1,840 units for $772.80, then 1,910 units for $592.10).

**Billing**

| Month | Account | Plan | Volume | Amount |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Jan | 1042 | standard | 1,840 | $772.80 |
| Feb | 1042 | no billing row | | |
| Mar | 1042 | enterprise-annual | 1,910 | $592.10 |
| Apr | 1077 | enterprise-annual | 1,120 | $347.20 |
| May | 1077 | enterprise-annual | 1,085 | $336.35 |
| Jun | 1077 | no billing row | | |

- Billed volume was about 1,840–1,910 in Jan and Mar and about 1,085–1,120 in Apr and May, so it dropped roughly 40% after the rename.
- The cause isn't in the data. It could be a real usage drop, a change in how volume is counted, or part of the usage moving elsewhere.
- Billed revenue fell from $772.80 in January to about $340 a month in April and May.

**Contract status**
- Status was active in Jan, paused in Feb, active in Mar, and active in Apr and May under the new ID.
- The Feb pause matches the missing Feb bill.
- There is no status row for June.

**Support tickets (6 total)**
- Under ACC-1042:
  - T-5033, a feature request opened 01-08.
  - T-5034, a feature request opened 03-11.
  - T-5035, an integration ticket opened 03-26.
- Under ACC-1077:
  - T-5036 and T-5037, both billing questions, opened 04-01 and 04-04. These came right after the rename and plan change, so they may be about the new billing.
  - T-5038, an outage report opened 05-25.
- There were no tickets in June or February.

**What the data can't tell you**
- **June:** there is no billing or contract-status row for ACC-1077. I can't tell whether the account churned, billing was late, or the extract is incomplete, so check that before calling it churn.
- **Reason for the pause:** the data doesn't say why it paused in February.
- **Whether ACC-1077 is a clean continuation:** it may be a rebrand or a merger. The name changed to "Health Partners", which could mean a wider entity, and the volume drop is unexplained.
- **Who gets the history:** if you query by account ID alone, ACC-1042 looks like it ended after March and ACC-1077 looks new. Any churn or new-logo count built on IDs would be wrong for this customer.

I didn't write any working files, since this only needed reading the six small files.
